basis: Defined by developmental impairment and epileptic encephalopathy; no established additional organ involvement.
Ear, CNS and cardiac malformations define the embryopathy; cleft palate occurs in 30-79%. Frequent nail hypoplasia omitted because of the cap.
Congenital neutropenia causes immunodeficiency; oral ulcers and destructive periodontal disease occur in 30-79%. Separately diagnosed infections excluded.
Inherited coagulation deficiency; supplied HPO reports intracranial and joint hemorrhage each in 30-79%, supporting direct brain and joint injury.
Organic acid metabolism disorders; neurologic injury is common in the major type I/II forms, supporting approximately >=30% overall. Muscle disease is subtype-dependent.
Isolated PLN-related dilated cardiomyopathy; cardiac disease in 20/20 patients.
Progressive cerebellar and movement disorder; oculomotor apraxia reflects neurologic dysfunction. Immunodeficiency and endocrine damage are not common defining features.
CNS hypomyelination defines disease; structural heart and hip/foot defects reported in 1/1 assessed each. Tiny denominators limit certainty; cerebral visual loss is neurologic.
Isolated androgenetic hair loss; androgen sensitivity does not establish endocrine gland disease.
HNF1A-related pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction causes monogenic diabetes; diabetic organ complications are separate diseases.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; neurologic injury and skeletal myopathy are common major presentations, plausibly >=30% each. Hepatic disease is subtype-dependent.
Defined by constitutional platelet abnormalities and neurodevelopmental impairment; developmental delay in 6/7. Hearing and cardiac defects are uncommon.
Dermatitis 2/2, villous atrophy 1/2 with chronic diarrhea 2/2, and pulmonary fibrosis 1/2 support direct injury. Oligoarthritis 1/2 omitted because of the cap.
TUBB2A-related structural brain malformations, seizures and severe neurodevelopmental impairment.
Primary skeletal myopathy with fatty replacement; ocular motor dysfunction reported in 1/1 assessed and ptosis in 1/2. Small cohort limits frequency certainty.
Autoimmune blistering skin disease; supplied HPO places oral mucosal blisters at 30-79%, supporting gastrointestinal mucosal involvement.
Mixed teratoma/seminoma is typically a testicular germ-cell tumour; reproductive organs have no axis. No covered site of origin is specified.
Tumour originates in the uterine corpus, a reproductive organ outside the axes; neuroectodermal histology does not establish nervous-system involvement.
Pyruvate metabolism defect causes lactic acidosis; developmental impairment in 17/17 and seizures in 30-79% support direct CNS dysfunction. Hepatomegaly is occasional.
Defined by progressive skeletal muscular dystrophy and early cardiac conduction disease, with possible cardiomyopathy and heart failure.
SPPL2A-related immunodeficiency with low IgG and mycobacterial susceptibility; BCG infection does not establish intrinsic damage to another organ axis.
Lung disease and brain abnormalities define syndrome; steatosis with elevated transaminases and pituitary/thyroid deficiency each in 1/1. Skeletal changes and anemia omitted by cap.
Primary breast carcinoma; breast has no axis. Receptor status does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Congenital abnormal communication between the aorta and right ventricle.
Bilateral inguinal hernia is a structural disorder involving herniation of abdominal contents; no additional organ damage is established.
